Container.Name: CamStack
Container.Overview: CamStack is a self-hosted camera-management hub. ONVIF/RTSP/Reolink/Hikvision device providers, a WebRTC and RTSP restream broker, recording, and a motion + ML detection pipeline, all as addons over a typed RPC layer. Run this once; add a CamStack Agent on any other machine whose GPU/NPU you want to put to work. The admin UI is HTTPS on port 4443 with a self-signed certificate by default. Map BOTH /data and /config, and set the admin credentials before first boot.

Config.Name: WebUI (HTTPS)
Config.Description: Admin UI and API over HTTPS. Self-signed by default.

Config.Name: Cluster transport (TCP)
Config.Description: Moleculer cluster transport between the hub and remote agents. Needed only for a multi-machine cluster.

Config.Name: Cluster discovery (UDP)
Config.Description: Moleculer same-subnet auto-discovery. Not needed when the hub address is set explicitly.

Config.Name: RTSP restream
Config.Description: RTSP restream served on demand by the stream broker.

Config.Name: WebRTC (TCP)
Config.Description: WebRTC media. Required for live view from outside the LAN.

Config.Name: WebRTC (UDP)
Config.Description: WebRTC media — the normal transport. Prefer UDP; TCP is the fallback.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Installed addons, ML models, TLS certificates, logs and the runtime SQLite database. Losing this loses the install.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: config.yaml — bootstrap server/auth/tls settings and the generated JWT secret. Kept separate from the data root so the one file worth backing up is easy to find.

Config.Name: Recordings
Config.Description: Recordings and event media. Point this at a roomy array share, not the cache. The paired CAMSTACK_MEDIA_ROOT variable is what actually sends media here — changing one without the other does nothing.

Config.Name: Coral USB (whole USB bus)
Config.Description: Coral USB Edge TPU. The whole bus is mapped, not one device node, because the accelerator re-enumerates from 1a6e:089a to 18d1:9302 when libedgetpu initialises. Paired with the --device-cgroup-rule flag. Remove if you have no Coral.

Config.Name: Intel/AMD GPU
Config.Description: Hardware video decode/encode (VAAPI/QSV) and OpenVINO GPU inference. Remove this if the machine has no integrated GPU — software decode costs roughly 60% of a CPU for a handful of 4K HEVC cameras.

Config.Name: Intel NPU
Config.Description: Intel NPU (OpenVINO) for ML inference. Remove if the machine has no NPU. The entrypoint chowns the device nodes to the container user on boot.

Config.Name: Node role
Config.Description: hub | agent. One image serves both; this selects the role at boot. Leave it as hub here.

Config.Name: Admin username
Config.Description: Admin login, seeded on first boot and reconciled every boot.

Config.Name: Admin password
Config.Description: Admin password. Set this before the first boot — an empty value falls back to the built-in default, which the UI then forces you to change.

Config.Name: JWT secret
Config.Description: Fixed signing secret so login sessions survive a restart. Leave blank to generate one into config.yaml. Generate: openssl rand -hex 32

Config.Name: Media root
Config.Description: Container path all media is written under. Must match the Recordings path above, or recordings land inside /data and fill the cache.

Config.Name: Hub public URL
Config.Description: Externally reachable base URL of this hub, e.g. https://192.168.1.9:4443. Remote agents fetch addon bundles and models from it. Leave blank only for a single-machine install — the https://127.0.0.1:4443 fallback is unreachable from an agent and silently breaks deploying addons to one.

Config.Name: Cluster: advertise hostname
Config.Description: Must stay false for a multi-machine cluster so nodes advertise their IP rather than a container hostname no other host can resolve.

Config.Name: Cluster: event fanout
Config.Description: Inter-node event delivery mode: filter | shadow | broadcast.

Config.Name: Frame-ring budget (MB)
Config.Description: Per-camera decoder frame-ring budget. Keep the aggregate under --shm-size. The code default is 16; change it only if you know why.
